chunks: He became independent in prominence and religious leadership after the death of his teacher al-Murtada, may his secret be sanctified.

key_terms.أُسْتَاذِهِ: his teacher — unambiguously al-Sharif al-Murtada in this biographical context
key_terms.الزَّعَامَةِ: leadership; specifically the supreme religious and juristic authority of the Shia community
key_terms.قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ: honorific formula for great deceased scholars: 'may his secret/soul be sanctified'

ai.seo_question: How did Shaykh al-Tusi assume religious leadership of the Shia community after the death of al-Sharif al-Murtada?
ai.summary: This biographical excerpt from the introductory chapter on Shaykh al-Ta'ifa records that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Tusi assumed sole, independent religious leadership of the Shia community following the death of his teacher al-Sharif al-Murtada ('Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Musawi) in 436 AH/1044 CE. The phrase قُدِّسَ سِرُّهُ is a Shia honorific for deceased scholars of the highest rank, paralleling رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ but carrying an additional spiritual connotation of inner sanctity.
